rv.q: Some forty years later, screaming and, indeed, discreet sobbing are actually the appropriate reactions to the ecstatic, quasi-immersive production of “Cats: The Jellicle Ball,” at PAC NYC.

The resulting production is a febrile—if scarcely feline—delight, an exuberant parade of song, dance, preening and posing that revitalizes Mr. Lloyd Webber's enduring score with wit, invention and roof-rattling energy.
Levingston and Rauch’s vision fits Cats like a long sequined glove.
Cats: The Jellicle Ball is queen (and kween) of this and all other nights.
It’s the musical event of the summer and the most fun I’ve ever had at an Andrew Lloyd Webber show.
Not only is this Cats different from any you have ever seen before, it is the most dynamic musical show to be seen in New York right now.
Imagine my surprise when Cats: The Jellicle Ball, the new adaptation of the material now at the Arts Center, turned out to be a plentiful source of dazzle, fun and joy.
Much care has been taken in the grafting of the queer onto the weird.
There’s no denying how much fun this production is – and how even a flawed show can find a path to rebirth via Eliot’s vaunted Heaviside Layer.

Come for the catchy songs, stay for the ballroom extravaganza, and remember that while the cast may be extravagant and constantly one-upping and over-the-topping each other, it’s not a feature or a bug, it’s the whole point.

cn.t: Critics praise this bold reinvention of Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical through the lens of ballroom culture, finding it a sensational and clever transformation that breathes new life into a show many found tired or confusing.

vr.q: I really cannot recommend this production enough. It's so creative, so well done, the directorial choices and overall concept is so smart, and the performances eat.
Cats: the Jellicle Ball is everything a revival should do this show is completely reimagined.
honestly whoever came up with this concept is a genius
This is the revival that you do not want to miss this summer. The hype surrounding this production is absolutely earned. I loved everything about this revival.

Here I am in the year of our Lord 2024 to tell you that a production of cats is actually good. I think that this production not only completely delivers on its premise, but is everything you wanted to be and more.
